## Native three-component demo and bounded REA outcomes — 2026-10-29

The standard-assembly demo was exercised in a separate visible Windows Electron
44.9.3 process with an owned fresh profile and the unchanged production main,

See the [combined walkthrough](DEMO_ASSEMBLIES.md#from-a-modeled-part-to-a-constrained-three-component-assembly)

An earlier isolated launch used `windowsHide:true` and produced no targetable
SolidFlow window. The subsequent visible launch used `windowsHide:false` with
the same products and became controllable. This changes only the private
launcher; it is a bounded observed launch comparison, not a production-window
fix or general platform conclusion. Unlike the earlier unexercised attempt,
this fresh process opened the saved three-component assembly through its real
native file dialog. The original fixture and source part remained unchanged;
all writes went to an owned copy. The native demo process was left open in its
own profile after the final checks.

Fifteen retained UI/accessibility checkpoints and four actual saved-file
proofs cover the following sequence. They are not a complete event-by-event
input log.

1. Open the original assembly and use native Save As to create a byte-identical
   owned copy. The original opened assembly was solved and canceled before
   creating the copy.
2. With native keyboard input, change the root-to-Guía signed distance from
   -40 to -45. Preview, Cancel and verify retained -45 draft fields with Apply
   revoked; retry, then Apply. Guía and Pin both move to X45.
3. Use Ctrl+S. Use Ctrl+Z and Save to restore the complete original bytes, then
   Ctrl+Y and Save to restore the complete edited bytes. Reopen that saved copy
   and inspect its components; solve and cancel the reopened copy again.
4. Click Guía and Pin in the actual 3D viewport and inspect their corresponding
   Properties panes. Displayed positions are Guía (45,0,approximately 0) and
   Pin (45,0,20), with Base still fixed at identity.
5. Exercise wheel inputs of +240 and -240 and Fit, observing the resulting
   views qualitatively.

The saved-file proof snapshots for Apply, Undo, Redo and reopening preserve
component IDs, definitions, fixed/visible state, captures and all relation
fields except the intended distance edit. The initial/Undo bytes have SHA-256
`fed4aee20af759c613ccc210a382f75e48ee741d074977c132b5d6353ea44091`;
Apply/Redo/reopened bytes have SHA-256
`d1c27a8afe074910784b3122bd20bf1a5e16d76898b5f30ab9b864b61a35e0d9`.
The largest saved-coordinate error against the literal X45 placement is below
1.12e-9 mm. The reopened native solve reports **zero local DOF, rank 12 and
four satisfied physical checks**. Residuals are satisfied, not numerically
zero: the retained native checks show linear residuals at most 6.66e-10 mm and
angular residuals at most 2.07e-11 rad.

This session adds native opening, editing, history, saving/reopening, component
selection and a fresh-process solve of the existing authored assembly. It does
not repeat native creation of every part/component/relation or prove every

were not archived as pixel-hashed native captures. No new BRep validity,
volume/area or STEP measurements are claimed beyond the separate automated
geometry evidence below. The bounded run does not establish human acceptance,
complete assembly parity, installed-platform support or release readiness.

### Observing the retained macOS face-click failure

The failed macOS face route had already passed ten native phases, its first
Save and all six held wheel/leave/Escape rejection cases. It failed at the
first saved second-face replacement toward the original inward cap at z-3:
the exact expected hover was observed and press/release was dispatched. The
recorder did not observe request closure within the existing 35-second step
deadline. There were
no reported console/resource errors. The retained report contains no
post-release DOM snapshot, so it does not establish whether a gesture guard,
changed scene/frame, hit target or application admission rejected the click.

The recorder now collects a bounded passive trace around each of its seven
existing accepted-click attempts. It retains before/event/after DOM metadata
and the last four existing worker-build headers. A ring holds at most sixteen
events with a dropped count; two independent flags retain whether canvas
down/up were observed even if older events leave the ring. Target tags and
window identity distinguish a genuine window blur from captured descendant
blur. Pointer endpoints delivered outside the canvas remain visible in the
trace. These listeners do not dispatch input, invoke application handlers or
change camera, geometry, tickets, deadlines, file grants or tolerances.

Event snapshots run in the capture phase before the canvas handler. The final
snapshot runs after the existing acceptance/build wait or its original error;
it is not an immediate post-handler probe. Listener/global cleanup runs in
`finally`, preserving the original failure if collection also fails. DOM reads
and observation transport can affect timing. A diagnostic pass therefore does
not establish a causal fix for the retained macOS failure.

The combined helper records **32 geometry checkpoints: 30 backed by native

Four ordered origin relations and two captured rotation locks constrain Guía
at (35,0,0) and Pin at (35,0,20), with Base fixed at identity. They use root X

Before Capture, it freezes the verified input quaternions and independently
computes their relative rotation with Hamilton algebra. The returned capture
and final orientation are checked against those earlier inputs. Pin bounds
come from eight literal original corners transformed by that retained input
rotation. Final XYZ, residual and zero-DOF checks remain strict.

scene; it does not independently measure restored displayed geometry. Reopen

## Dedicated CAD worker channel admission — 2026-10-27

The worker entry now checks actual channel metadata before reading message data
or calling the existing serial queue. It accepts browser-delivered dedicated
events with empty origin, null source and no transferred ports. Synthetic events
are ignored without closing their caller-owned ports; actual received extra
ports are closed and their request is withheld. The existing envelope, payload,
queue serialization and private session capabilities remain. This hardening
does not authenticate a compromised owning renderer or establish a prior
exploitable cross-window vulnerability. The [development contract](DEVELOPMENT.md#dedicated-worker-message-admission--2026-10-27)
links the applicable WHATWG channel and MessageEvent semantics.

Nine new units import the real worker entry with mocked queue/dispatcher/native
dependencies. They check payload identity and continued queue admission of null,
rejection of synthetic events and unexpected origin/source metadata before any
data getter, closure of both actually received test ports and retention of
synthetic caller-owned ports. On the old entry, eight fail and the accepted-path
case passes; with the guard all nine pass. Together with existing queue and
standard/configured transport cases, five files pass 97/97 and TypeScript passes.
Units do not establish browser provenance, native BRep behavior or actual
MessagePort closure inside a compiled worker.

passes after rebuilding the guard. Port closure itself is asserted by units;

One hosted Windows sphere case previously rejected the atomic rename for its
fourth Save with `EPERM`: its submitted canonical document matched the expected authored
snapshot, while disk retained the third successful Save. That evidence does
not identify the denying process/permission or explain every earlier deadline.

six attempts on the same already-synced and closed temporary file. Five scheduled
waits total 1,550 ms. It never removes/truncates/copies over the old destination.

retried. The main-frame sender is checked before each attempt. A check cannot
cancel an OS rename already submitted; this change adds no such claim.

exact byte views, bounds, other errors/platform branches, sender invalidation,

cleanup error that must not mask publication failure. The platform-branch cases
are simulations on Windows, not Linux/macOS runtime evidence. The real Windows
case opens only its own original temporary fixture without Delete sharing,
observes the first denied rename, closes that reader and publishes exact new
bytes on retry. It is skipped on non-Windows hosts.

## Configured origin and background contexts — 2026-10-27

selection of its component owner. Background offers nine orientations, Normal

the selection. Labels use current occurrence names; IDs remain authority keys.

purpose-compatible form option in the current edit frame. The scope root maps

preview, camera-navigation and dialog guards remain. Keyboard viewport context
now resolves one selected current origin before an older component selection;
multiple origins or mixed face/origin selection retain background commands.
Missing, duplicate or stale origin catalogs cannot silently retarget a component.

and YZ normal +X, the expected second X coordinate is -60 mm; the saved value
differed by approximately 2.56e-10 mm. The first occurrence stayed fixed at
the origin; the second retained Y=Z=0 and identity rotation.

Native Save As, switching to the standalone part, and native Open of the
related assembly preserved both occurrences and both relations. A fresh solve
reported one remaining local degree of freedom and rank five. The coincidence
reported zero linear/angular residual; the distance reported 2.56e-10 mm and
zero angular residual against displayed limits of 1e-6 mm and 1e-8 rad.

the separately saved part, and its displayed combined volume was 60,390.385 mm3.

## Two-direction and mid-plane revolution — 2026-10-25

The optional saved extent distinguishes two independently entered angles from a
mid-plane total angle. A two-direction side may be zero, but both values must be
finite and nonnegative and their sum must be greater than zero and no more than
360 degrees. Mid-plane and absent unilateral extent require a positive angle
at most 360 degrees. Invalid declarations fail without clamping or fallback.
Mid-plane ignores reversal for geometry and reference identity while preserving
the saved reverse choice. Leaving Direction 2 or choosing mid-plane discards
the second angle; returning to unilateral mode removes the extent field.

Focused validation passes 67 core cases, 21 UI cases and 130 model/document
cases in their respective selected groups, including legacy regressions. These
are group totals, not counts of newly added cases or a complete-suite result.
The production build passes in 3.562 s. All 1,117 frozen non-Markdown source
inputs match the isolated runtime checkout. The first executions of all three
selected production renderers pass on local Windows with Node 24.11.1 and
Electron 44.9.3:

| Workflow | Checkpoints | Elapsed |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Revolution, two-direction/mid-plane previews and saved editing | 178 | 48.633 s |
| Successive part operations | 118 | 31.371 s |
| Fresh face-supported sketch | 48 | 16.243 s |

All three report zero console, request and resource errors, confirmed child exit
and isolated-profile cleanup. Final local `npm test` passes in 546.082 s:
9,699 unit/CAD cases across 422 files, plus 83 passing IPC checks and two
explicit skips. `npm run test:desktop` passes in 1.599 s with zero console,
request and resource errors. The same 1,117 frozen inputs cover the build,
three selected renderers, full suite and desktop smoke. These local results do
not establish a complete renderer/platform matrix or current-head hosted success.

The revolution renderer checks a zero second side, asymmetric 60/30-degree
previews in both senses, mid-plane total 90 degrees, return to an absent
unilateral extent, rejection above 360 degrees and correction to 270/90.
It preserves committed recovery across previews and rejection, then saves the
reversed 270/90 full turn with its subsequent bore. History, reopening both
angle controls and the independent STEP read pass. Mid-plane is previewed and
cancelled; its persistence is covered by model tests, not this saved renderer
case. Commands use actual Chromium pointer input; numeric/select changes remain

## Saved feature recipe regeneration — local source checkpoint (2026-10-14)

Source commit [97def5ae](https://github.com/angelcp2802/solidflow/commit/97def5ae2ab0b3e15fc007f560cecd465b9c138d)
connects strict saved declarations, explicit-frame tools, chronological native
evaluation and staged body/catalog/cache adoption. The branch changes 36 paths
from base [d0173137](https://github.com/angelcp2802/solidflow/commit/d01731374b08b3031f5b54e6012dfaf8aa54c6c4).
The final validation map has 271 runtime inputs. Their bytes were checked against
the committed Git tree; the map SHA-256 is
`5e80aa6bf96658a88c83e722962f0f6a1bfd637abb92ebae18694f181adc76c1`.
Dependencies and the lockfile are unchanged. This documentation update does not
change those runtime inputs.

### Implemented and checked scope

Explicit feature patterns can choose geometry copying or regeneration. Initial
regeneration accepts selected exact current targets and historical source
poststates, intrinsic rectangle/circle cut or merge operations, blind/ThroughAll
endings, no reference policies and no variation. Actual tools rebuild against
progressive working owners in canonical instance and saved feature order.
Selected parents have same-address semantic roles even when their material is
unchanged. Changed final owners publish atomically; unchanged owners retain their
old references. Geometry copying remains a separate method, with no fallback for
failed regeneration.

The [fixture provenance](PROVENANCE.md#chronological-recipe-evaluator-fixtures)
and [regeneration contract](FEATURE_REGENERATION.md) give the exact dimensions,
formulas, tolerances and limits. Standalone evaluator and saved-engine geometric
cases check BRep validity, final solid count, volume, area and bounds; selected
cases add independent material
probes. Metric tolerance is 1e-5 mm³/mm², coordinate tolerance 1e-6 mm and probe
volume tolerance 1e-7 mm³. These tolerances do not establish general robustness.

saved instance identities, committed retirement and one atomic new-body or
targeted-merge transaction. [PROVENANCE](PROVENANCE.md) gives the original
analytical coordinates, formulas, units and tolerances. Earlier evidence below
retains its original source scope and does not validate this increment.

of parametric history/body IDs through STEP. The initial catalog policy rejects
empty, disconnected or split outputs requiring undeclared body identities.
At that earlier source, sweep, loft and repetition producers still needed
explicit body-output ownership.

## Evidence scope

The public repository uses a self-contained suite. Claims are limited to the
cases checked, with the tolerances recorded in each test.

| Command | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run test:unit` | Sketch geometry, solver, documents, CAD operations and saved UI fixtures |
| `npm run test:ipc` | Main-process IPC security and boundary checks |
| `npm run build` | TypeScript compilation and production Vite build |
| `npm run test:desktop` | Real Electron production page, preload, worker, WASM and first solid |
| `npm run package:<platform>` | Packaging for the host OS, without publication |

CAD checks use known coordinates, analytical formulas, valid BRep/solid counts,
volume, area, bounds and relevant Boolean differences. A matching volume alone
is insufficient evidence of identical geometry. Saved documents are parsed and
rebuilt; UI-export fixtures are identified separately from programmatic outputs.

GitHub Actions runs the portable suite, build, IPC and Electron smoke on
Windows x64, macOS arm64 and Linux x64, and packages each platform. Its actual
runs are authoritative; workflow configuration alone does not establish a pass.
CodeQL and a dependency audit run separately. The audit includes development
dependencies, blocks high/critical findings and leaves moderate findings visible.

Development packages are unsigned. Successful packaging does not establish
successful installation, notarization or all interactive workflows on that OS.
The project does not yet have exhaustive topology, numerical robustness,
accessibility, performance or platform coverage.

Local evidence for this increment is from Windows x64 with Node 24.11.1.
The nine new CAD cases passed in a focused run. TypeScript/Vite production
build passed with the existing large-chunk and dependency-externalization
warnings. The first complete unit run finished with 1,380 passed and 112

seconds: 1,431 passed and 61 timed out (60 at 5 seconds, one at 30 seconds),
across 14 failed and 60 passed files. IPC did not run because the unit command
failed. Test selection, assertions and existing timeout budgets were unchanged.
Running `npm run test:ipc` separately then passed all 11 checks, with no failures,
cancellations or skips; this does not change either failed complete-suite result.
The first local Electron smoke exited at its existing 45-second limit before
readiness was established. One retry after the complete unit runs had terminated
also exited at the unchanged 45-second limit without establishing readiness.
No complete local-suite or local-loader pass is claimed for this increment.
A bounded resource observation found significant external CPU load, but it
does not establish the sole cause of these outcomes.

A fresh isolated `npm ci` passed from the 0.19.0 manifest and lockfile, whose
hashes remained unchanged. Audit reported eight moderate findings and zero
high/critical findings; none was suppressed.

All six required hosted checks passed on source head `65104a3`:
[desktop CI](https://github.com/angelcp2802/solidflow/actions/runs/38309109057),
[security](https://github.com/angelcp2802/solidflow/actions/runs/38309109062)
and [CodeQL](https://github.com/angelcp2802/solidflow/runs/115010656069).
Each desktop job passed all 1,492 portable tests in 74 files and all 11 IPC
checks, with no skips, plus build, real initial-model Electron smoke and
unsigned packaging. Smoke logs report WASM loaded, zero console errors and
zero failed requests. Windows x64 and Linux x64 used Node 24.21.0; macOS arm64
used Node 24.20.0. These are results for the recorded source and workflows,
not exhaustive platform or interactive-tool validation. Subsequent heads
still require their own checks before merge.

The original Cartesian CAD fixture is a 50×20 mm plate, 4 mm deep, with
two circular holes. Their source radii 3 and 5 mm, separated by 20 mm, share
an outward offset of 2 mm, giving hole radii 5 and 7 mm. Independent planar
area and perimeter are `S=1000−π(rA²+rB²)` and `P=140+2π(rA+rB)`;
the prism uses `V=4S` and `A=2S+4P`. At radii 5 and 7 this gives
`V=4000−296π` mm³ and `A=2560−52π` mm². Tests check both selection
orders, one programmatic history entry, undo/redo, exact document reopening,
valid BRep, one solid, bounds and fresh programmatic STEP export/reimport.

A second plate starts with source radii 2 and 5 mm and offset 1 mm. Shared
distance 1→1.5 and source radius 2→2.25 edits rebuild the analytical solid.
Unchanged exterior face/edge references and an R1 exterior-corner fillet
survive these particular edits. That fillet independently removes
`4−π` mm³ and `10−2.5π` mm². Resized circular rims and perforated faces
currently receive different geometric keys: a saved rim fillet rejects its
stale selection and export is blocked rather than silently selecting another
edge. General persistent naming remains open in
[issue #21](https://github.com/angelcp2802/solidflow/issues/21).

No-dimension, driven-dimension and deleted-dimension cases check a shared
offset changed through an image-radius constraint. A larger shared offset
whose circles cross the plate boundary rejects the solid without modifying
the input or exporting a stale result. Coordinates and radii use `5e-7` mm;
mass, area and bounds use absolute `5e-6` in their respective units. Healthy
solver residuals must stay within the existing `1e-7` acceptance. The new
CAD cases use a 60-second per-case budget for WASM reconstruction; geometric
criteria and production solver tolerances were not relaxed.

Core and planner coverage includes shared distance families, strict saved
references, deletion cleanup, disconnected component partitioning, per-chain
direction, atomic capacity/rejection and both-side cap coupling. Dimension
ownership, driven/deleted-dimension edits and cap coupling are explicit local
policies; equivalence to another solver is not established. Server rendering
and source review are separate from actual pointer, keyboard, cancel and
interactive history/reopening, which remain unexecuted for the new tool.
The Electron smoke exercises only the initial model. STEP producer and reader
share OpenCascade, so these round trips do not establish independent
interoperability. Broader offset coverage remains open in
[issue #14](https://github.com/angelcp2802/solidflow/issues/14), and binary
upload remains disabled under
[issue #5](https://github.com/angelcp2802/solidflow/issues/5).

## Owned STEP import increment — 2026-10-11

On Windows x64 with Node 24.11.1, `npm test` passed all 1,247 portable tests in
61 files and all 11 IPC checks, without skips. `npm run build` passed with the
existing dependency-externalization and large-chunk warnings. The real Electron
production-loader smoke passed with `wasmLoaded: true`, `consoleErrors: []` and
`failedRequests: []`. This smoke exercises the initial solid, not STEP file
selection or the import controls. An isolated fresh `npm ci` installed all
341 packages successfully. The dependency audit reported 0 high/critical and
8 moderate development findings; none is suppressed.

This increment adds 126 portable cases and 3 IPC checks. They cover exact owned
bytes, canonical base64, SHA-256 integrity and the 8 MiB source boundary;
strict additive version-1 parsing; first-solid and single-import ownership;
history, suppression, deletion and reference dependencies; and atomic import
preparation. Transaction cases reject malformed files, failed construction,
cancelled replacement and stale document/edit contexts before a commit.
Transport checks resend the complete source after worker replacement and
export a committed snapshot independently of another build. Real main-process
handlers, with controlled dialog transport and temporary files, check bounded
reads, exact bytes, sender identity, operation serialization and absence of a
write grant for the original STEP. These controlled checks are separate from
actual editor and native-dialog interaction, which remains unverified for this
increment.

The ten original inputs, generator and manifest are described in
[PROVENANCE.md](PROVENANCE.md). Accepted cases check a box, translation,
rotation, a true cylindrical BRep, declared inch conversion and declared metre
conversion against analytical expectations. Open shells, multiple solids,
free topology outside the solid, truncated input and an unsupported native
geometric entity reject. A closed-shell gate, BRep validity, positive volume,
one solid and complete root transfer are required. Cleanup tests check that
repeated success/failure leaves no temporary virtual import file.

The [STEP contract](STEP_IMPORT.md) records independent formulas for the
10×6×4 mm box (`V=240 mm³`, `A=248 mm²`), cylinder and unit conversions.
An imported top face supports a through-hole at `(5,3)` with radius 1 mm:
`V=240−4π` and `A=248+6π`. Editing its radius to 1.5 mm after reopening gives
`V=240−9π` and `A=248+15π/2`. A selected imported edge supports an R1 fillet.
Checks include exact source-byte reopening, face/edge reference stability,
reference invalidation after source replacement, downstream reconstruction,
suppression/deletion, undo/redo and programmatic STEP export/reimport.
Absolute mass/area/bounds tolerances are `5e-6` in their respective units;
coordinate-based selected-edge checks use `5e-7` mm. Public fixtures and round
trips use the same OpenCascade runtime for generation and consumption; they do
not establish interoperability with an independent producer or kernel.

The bounded Part 21 unit gate follows referenced 3D representation contexts
and conversion factors. It accepts SI millimetres, SI metres and declared
25.4 mm conversion units; missing, malformed, conflicting and unsupported
length declarations reject. Strings, comments and unused contexts cannot
supply a missing unit. External-resource entities and additional sections
reject before native transfer. The gate is not a full EXPRESS schema validator
and does not establish support for arbitrary STEP schemas, assemblies or
metadata. Source bytes remain embedded in the editable document; no original
path, native handle or worker cache is required to reopen it.

Hosted checks are pending for this increment's exact source head. Earlier
platform results do not establish a pass for these changes. Binary publication
remains disabled under [issue #5](https://github.com/angelcp2802/solidflow/issues/5).

## Releasable line-offset endpoint following — 2026-10-12

On Windows x64 with Node 24.11.1, `npm test` passed 1,441 portable tests in
71 files and all 11 IPC checks, with no skips. TypeScript/Vite build passed
with the existing dependency-externalization and large-chunk warnings. The
isolated Electron production-loader smoke passed with WASM loaded, zero
console errors and zero failed requests; it exercises the initial model.
Fresh isolated `npm ci` installed 341 packages. Its dependency graph and
manifest match this source except for root version metadata, changed from
0.17 to 0.18 after installation. Audit: eight moderate, zero high/critical.

The 62 added cases comprise 28 core, 28 explicit-reposition and 6 CAD checks.
New no-dimension uncapped line boundaries follow independently until an
accepted explicit point edit releases the requested boundary. Checks cover
untouched source length 10→14, released end x=12, released start x=-2 with
untouched end continuing to 14, normal-only release, reversed traversal,
rotated 3-4-5 geometry, mixed line/arc boundaries and independent sides.
Strict parsing preserves false flags, rejects malformed/ineligible states
and keeps legacy absence/free mode and permanent aligned mode unchanged.
Output constraints remain hard targets; they may drive a free source or
reject a fixed-source conflict without implicitly releasing a boundary.
Local reported DOF is tested; equivalence to another solver is not claimed.

The explicit command uses the solved profile displayed to the user and rejects
stale or unhealthy sources. Full XY targets and partial X/Y targets are tested
against existing relations, including an R10 circle where X=8 permits Y=6.
Temporary target points/constraints are removed before saved rank and driven
values are calculated. Invalid IDs, origin edits, nonfinite/out-of-range
coordinates, capacity overflow and conflicting targets reject atomically.
Targets within `5e-7` mm of their current coordinate preserve following and
avoid a history write. Final requested axes must also remain within `5e-7`
mm after temporary target removal; a small equation residual alone cannot
confirm a point destination. A near-parallel support regression rejects a
request whose cleaned solution moves away from its target. A successful
release survives one programmatic undo/redo entry and saved-document reopening.
App wiring calls the command from the canvas and numeric point inspector;
focused component checks are server rendering, not pointer/keyboard execution.

The original Cartesian fixture builds a width-2, height-4 prism through two

budget. For a unit circle directed toward (0,2), the full GN step is
2cos(theta); near pi/2 it almost reflects the error while making an arbitrarily
small cost improvement. Accepting any decrease converged too slowly.

The corrected source requires Armijo 0.1 sufficient decrease against the
predicted first-order reduction of the actual clipped/backtracked step. Every
secondary acceptance retains the best primary cost within a fixed roundoff
band; secondary improvement cannot bypass insufficient primary progress.
The same geometric expectations and default 80-iteration/16-trial budgets remain;
one stricter eight-iteration hinge case was added. Requested mate tolerances and
stationarity policy were not relaxed. All eight commands passed on the final
tested source; no later production-code drift is claimed equivalent to it.

### Numerical and independent native evidence

The pointer uses an explicitly separate soft objective. Translation prioritizes
selected world position, rotation prioritizes orientation; native saved mates
remain mandatory. Checked hard-Jacobian nullspaces supply the available motion.
Normal scope rank/DOF never includes a pointer anchor. Bounded finite secondary
cost-tie probes handle the unit-circle centre case, where all positions have
equal primary cost. A conditioned pure case retains a unit local offset near
origin (1e16,0,0); it does not establish native accuracy at that physical scale,
which the native adapter's coordinate-resolution policy rejects.

Actual native cases establish:

- A concentric slider with an authenticated spin lock projects requested
  (13,4,z+5) onto (10,0,z+5), preserving one axial DOF and reporting pointer
  distance 5. Removing the spin lock retains two DOF and also reaches secondary
  Z90, with native eccentric-bore/material probes. The same off-axis target
  remains rejected by both strict movement APIs.
- A fixed payload at local (1,0,0) belongs to a floating rigid owner whose native
  cylinder/cap mates leave Z spin. Position target (0,2,0) projects to
  (0,1,0)/Z90, distance 1. Rotation priority retains requested Z90 while moving
  the selected origin, reporting distance sqrt(2). The initially unsolved child
  case solves its plane first and derives the circle radius from that genuinely
  solved child frame; its underdetermined X/Y coordinates are not assumed nominal.
- A free relative-lock pair moves together and retains six natural local DOF.
  Source/history/reopen, suppressed/fixed identity, source build/release
  failure and actual numerical-output corruption cases withhold unauthorized
  publication. No-op or blocked movement grants no capability.

Placed R2 pins remain BRep-valid, one solid each, V189pi/4 and A495pi/8 within
1e-5. Bounds/positions use 1e-6, target angles 1e-8 and 0.1 mm cube/Common
probe volumes 1e-7 around zero or 0.001. These separate native measurements do
not become UI material queries, collision-free mechanism proof or a material
union across overlapping component occurrences.
The unreachable hinge's expected quarter-turn basis/error comparisons use
1e-6; the 1e-8 angular policy applies to hard checks, native/numerical frame
agreement and reachable requested orientation. No optimizer error bound is
inferred from those hard tolerances.

## All-use subassembly source revisions and explicit descendant repair

This local increment is based on `3fe9923` and adds a complete embedded assembly
source-update route. An incoming v2 document must retain the selected source ID
and declare a different revision. The model merges the complete normalized
registry, reuses only exact tuple/content matches, retains old definitions and
retargets only occurrence addresses recorded before importing. Shared,
suppressed and dormant declarations are included. A conflicting dependency that
would alias a host scope being rewritten rejects. Existing graph, feature and
pretty UTF-8 document limits remain in force.

Affected mate roles are found by traversing their full old path through the
source boundary, including when the terminal part tuple stays unchanged. All
affected roles require explicit current descendant choices or explicit mate
removal. The private worker retains the source plan and native catalog; mutable
review/scene replies, renderer candidates and repaired flags confer no Apply
authority. Captured relations require explicit recapture/removal, with an
additional release option for concentric spin locks. The source-local catalog
includes suppressed descendants in a separate inspection copy; it is not a
claim of solved inactive placements or dormant relations.

The 41 new public cases comprise 14 declaration, 15 native/session, ten rendered
panel and two transport cases. Native cases check two copies of an original
2×3×4 mm prism (`V=24`, `A=52`) updated to 3×3×4 mm (`V=36`, `A=66`), with inner
Rz90 and translation `(1,2,3)` and outer X translations -10/+20 mm. Updated
bounds are `[-12,2,3]..[-9,5,7]` and `[18,2,3]..[21,5,7] mm`. The pair totals
`V=72 mm³`, `A=132 mm²`; a separate old-source occurrence remains unchanged.
Volume and area bands are `1e-5`, and bounds use `1e-6 mm`. Other cases include
an ancestor-only placement change with unchanged terminal tuple, renamed-child
repair, all four saved centered-Width roles, declaring null frames, suppressed
references, actual component-lock recapture and actual suppressed-concentric
spin recapture with restored suppression. Source query and release faults
withhold the entire review and invalidate an older capability.

The dedicated production-renderer workflow uses the two tracked original
source-update fixtures. Two source uses change to a new part revision and a
renamed child, while a direct old part remains unchanged. Independent total
material expectations are `V=72/A=156` before and `V=96/A=184` after, in cubic
and square millimeters, with the same bands above. The workflow selects two
explicit principal-plane repairs and checks four fresh physical relations in
the root and expanded source scopes. Review Cancel/retry, ready-preview
Cancel/retry, Apply, one Undo/Redo, parent normal Save, Save As/reopen and a fresh
solve all execute through production controls and the real worker. Wrong source
identity rejects without altering the committed recovery. Five Open and two
Save As dialogs use test-owned paths; native dialog pointer operation is not
tested. The first attempt stopped at an incorrect test-harness Save-dialog
